newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Rwanda tribunal detains four suspects for 30 days.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda tribunal detains four suspects for 30 days.

text.p: A tribunal on Rwanda's genocide on Monday extended for 30 days the detention of four suspects, including the first non-Rwandan to appear before the court.
Judge Laity Kama, president of the tribunal, said he was ordering the extension from Monday to ensure the four did not evade justice and in view of the complexity of investigations.

The four, who appeared before the tribunal last Thursday, included Belgian George Ruggiu, 40, who worked as a journalist and presenter for Rwanda's Radio Television des Milles Collines (RTLM) in Kigali during the three-month genocide in 1994.
The prosecution said when Ruggiu was arrested in Nairobi last month that he had a South African passport but had changed his identity and physical appearance, apparently to evade capture.

The other three were Sylvain Nsabimana, a former government official in the southern Rwandan city of Butare, Gratien Kabiligi, a former colonel in the army's general staff, and Aloys Ntabakuze, a former commander of a commando battalion.

Kama said he would rule later this week on whether detention should be extended for a fifth suspect, Rwandan journalist Hassan Ngeze. The prosecution said when he was arrested in Kenya last month he had several passports and was well-connected.
His defence lawyers opposed the extension, saying he wanted to clear his name and was unlikely to disappear if released.
Ngeze appeared in court on Monday but refused to answer questions from the prosecution about an affidavit he had made.

The tribunal, which has its headquarters in the northern Tanzanian town of Arusha, on Thursday extended the detention of former Rwandan prime minister Jean Kambanda for 30 days after he made no objection.
The six who all appeared in court on Thursday have not yet been indicted by the tribunal but are suspected of taking part in the 1994 genocide of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates.
The six have already been detained for an initial 30 days.
The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda was set up in 1994 to bring to justice leaders of the 1994 genocide sparked by the assassination of military strongman Juvenal Habyarimana.
A total of 21 suspects are held in Arusha. Three trials are now going on and 23 suspects have been indicted.
